analysis:
This PR changes only docs/reference/configuration.md. It adds two rows near head lines 415-416 for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED. Both are documented as default-on and forwarded to the LaunchAgent. No executable code, key handling, attestation, coordinator authorization or storage behavior changes in the supplied evidence. I reviewed both base units (lines 1-518, with lines 415-416 as the insertion point) and the patch excerpt.

Security-relevant observations, all documentation-level:
- The tool-call row says streaming `tool_choice` auto calls are sent as OpenAI `tool_calls` fragments before the call is fully validated. It states that each call is still validated when its frame closes. Partial, not-yet-validated tool-call fragments could reach the consumer if validation later fails. This touches response integrity on the coordinator/provider/consumer path (TB-002, T-007, T-008). The supplied evidence has no code showing validation bypass, encryption bypass or plaintext fallback. Streaming chunks must still pass through the existing per-chunk E2E encryption path (fail-closed per T-008). The real implementation, ToolStreamPreparation.swift, is not supplied.
- The think-content seed row changes reasoning parsing, so the answer streams earlier. It could affect where reasoning content is placed in the stream. No security boundary is evident in the supplied text.
- Neither variable concerns A-001, the keys, or the prefix cache (T-041), and neither is an attestation input.

Remaining integration questions for any code review: whether the streamed tool-call fragment path reuses the encrypted SSE chunk emitter, and whether a downstream consumer relying on tool_calls assumes completed validation. Neither is verifiable from this docs-only diff. No regression is established, so there are no findings.
